key_insight: The paper experimentally demonstrates nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity (NAQI): local measurements can steer a partner qubit into conditional states with imaginarity exceeding the classical bound.
engineering_relevance: This provides a measurable new nonclassical resource and a practical benchmark for quantum photonic control, state characterization, and resource-based quantum protocol design.
method: Prepared polarization-encoded two-qubit Bell-diagonal states in a photonic experiment.
Used the l1-norm of imaginarity inequality as the operational witness for NAQI.
Applied a hybrid genetic algorithm + sequential quadratic programming method to optimize measurement settings and avoid local optima.
evidence_signal: The experiment reported clear violations of the l1-norm imaginarity inequality for two classes of two-qubit states, and mapped the state regions showing \(\mathcal{D}_{\rm NAQC}\subset\mathcal{D}_{\rm NAQI}\subset\mathcal{D}_{\rm BN}\) for Werner states.
watch_item: The result depends on experimentally prepared Bell-diagonal photonic states and inequality-based witnesses, so performance and generality may vary with noise, state family, and measurement optimization quality.
paper_title: Experimental certification of the nonlocal advantages of quantum imaginarity
